status: Implemented and locally tested. Requires migration, server/client environment, scheduled delivery and physical-device acceptance before claiming live delivery.

serverEnvironment.WEB_PUSH_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY: Public P-256 VAPID key from web-push.generateVAPIDKeys()
serverEnvironment.WEB_PUSH_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY: Private key; server secret only. Generate once, never log or commit, retain across deployments.
serverEnvironment.WEB_PUSH_VAPID_SUBJECT: A real mailto: contact or HTTPS app/contact URL
serverEnvironment.CRON_SECRET: Existing or new secret shared only with the scheduler

clientEnvironment.VITE_MARRIAGE_WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY: The matching PUBLIC VAPID key only

schedule.deploymentOwnerAction: Vercel Pro plan verified by root. admin/vercel.json schedules /api/push every minute alongside the existing daily maintenance job; deployment activates the schedule. Keep CRON_SECRET configured so Vercel supplies the authenticated request.
schedule.latency: With minute scheduling, up to approximately one minute plus provider/device delivery. This is not a latency guarantee; an offline device, OS settings, focus mode or queue backlog can delay delivery.
schedule.capacity: 20 claimed jobs per invocation total (10 per transport if APNs and Web Push are both enabled). Monitor backlog/expiry and increase invocation frequency before expanding the pilot.
schedule.guard: Worker runs only on Vercel production and the dedicated Nisfayn project. Preview deployments return push_not_configured. APNs can remain disabled independently.

behavior: iPhone/iPad: use an OS supporting Web Push for Home Screen apps (iOS/iPadOS 16.4+), add Nisfayn to the Home Screen, open from that icon, sign in and explicitly enable notifications in Settings.
Supported desktop and Android browsers can enable Web Push directly from Settings; support is feature-detected.
Permission is requested only from the user's enable action. Existing permitted subscriptions refresh on return to the app.

Notifications cover requests, mutual acceptance and unread messages. Family rooms, journey changes, profile visits and incoming calls retain their current in-app behavior; this change does not claim background calling.
Generic Arabic notifications contain event kind and opaque request ID only. Names, message contents, photos and assessment answers are never sent to push providers.
Service worker handles push and notification clicks only. It has no fetch handler, offline content cache, auth token storage or API caching.

Subscriptions live in the existing private, RLS-enabled device table, bound to a live Auth session. Ownership, relationship eligibility and opt-in are rechecked before delivery. Account deletion, session revocation, opt-out, blocking and read/deleted messages stop pending sends.
A delivered OS notification cannot be recalled from every device. Local logout cleanup removes the browser subscription and closes notifications on that device.

Provider endpoints are explicitly allowlisted at registration and delivery to prevent server-side request forgery. Invalid/expired subscriptions are removed; transient failures use existing bounded retry/lease logic.
acceptance: Two approved real pilot accounts, separate devices/browsers; subscribe, close recipient app, send a request/message, confirm delivery and click to correct account's chat.
On iPhone, test the installed Home Screen app while backgrounded and while the phone is locked; deny permission and verify clear recovery guidance.
Test opt-out, logout, account switch and blocked/ended relationship; confirm no new pending notifications arrive for the old account.
Read or delete a message before the delivery cycle; verify no stale push is sent.
Verify /sw.js, manifest and icon return correct types; monitor worker failures and outbox expired/failed outcomes without logging endpoint URLs or encryption keys.
